description.narrative: Projektet utgår från frågeställningen om hur klimatpåverkan bidrar nya sårbarheter som växlar upp redan existerande, såsom långsam ekonomisk tillväxt, knappa naturresurser och bräckliga förvaltningsstrukturer. Forskningen kommer att ägna särskild uppmärksamhet åt huruvida existerande förvaltningsstrukturer i regionen bidrar till bristen på inkludering samt avsaknaden av åtgärder för att motverka klimatförändringar. Projektet kommer också att studera civilsamhällets organisationers roll att utifrån ett sårbarhetsperspektiv driva på klimatåtgärder på regional nivå.

The project approaches the question on how climatic impacts introduce new sets of vulnerabilities that accelerates already existing ones like slow economic growth, scarce natural resources, and fragile governance structures. The research will give particular attention to how current governance arrangements in the region are responsible for the lack of inclusivity and action towards climate change. The project will also study the role of civil society organisations in pushing climate action at a regional level from a vulnerability perspective.

The project "Climate Change, Vulnerability and Governance in the Middle East and North Africa" is a research initiative proposed for the period January 2022 - December 2023, with a budget of 830,000 USD or approximately 9 million SEK. The project approaches the question on how climatic impacts introduce new sets of vulnerabilities that accelerates already existing ones like slow economic growth, scarce natural resources, and fragile governance structures. The research will give particular attention to how current governance arrangements in the region are responsible for the lack of inclusivity and action towards climate change. The project will also study the role of civil society organisations in pushing climate action at a regional level from a vulnerability perspective.

- The project focused on connecting climate researchers, civil society actors, government officials, and other stakeholders to address climate change challenges in the MENA region. This included hosting a virtual "Climate Change Challenges in the Middle East and North Africa" workshop, as well as organized six study group sessions, focusing on various climate-sensitive sectors and stakeholders. A regional climate vulnerability conference was also hosted in Amman.
- The project produced research publications to fill knowledge gaps and provide analyses and recommendations for climate governance in the MENA region. An in-depth case study of climate change in Egypt with policy recommendations was published. Additionally, a climate compendium with eight articles on diverse climate-related topics in the MENA region was prepared, set for early 2024 publication.
- The project developed audio-visual content to transform public debates and provide in-depth technical conversations on climate change in the MENA region. This included recording 10 episodes of the Arabic language climate podcast "Darajten w Bas" and conducting five bilingual interviews with climate experts on MENA region challenges and opportunities.
- The project created a public database to present key climate risk, vulnerability, and governance data, making it easily accessible for various stakeholders. A project plan for a public climate data database focusing on risks, vulnerabilities, and governance was developed. Significant climate adaptation indicators were identified using Algeria as a sample profile. The project also planned the publication of database sets and accompanying articles for six MENA countries by the end of 2024.
